scenes.title: Cold open
narration: The Gourd Dance is defined by a 'howl' at the end of each song, a sonic tribute to the red wolf who, according to Kiowa legend, first taught the dance to a man lost in the wilderness.
This is Gourd Dance. 1957 revival.
on_screen: Title card: Gourd Dance · USA · 1957 revival

scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The dance originated from a Kiowa legend involving a red wolf.
It was once part of the Sun Dance but was suppressed by the U.S. government in the late 19th century.
It was formally revived in 1957.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: The dance is held during summer ceremonials, often around July 4.
It is a sacred tradition that signifies 'ready to go, ready to die' in the Kiowa language.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: Performed in a circular arena.
Men dance in a perimeter, lifting feet to the drumbeat and shaking rattles.
Women dance in place behind the men.
Watch for Stationary dance.
on_screen: Captions name each signature move as it appears

scenes.title: Listen
narration: The music consists of songs accompanied by a drum and metal rattles.
The tempo typically progresses from slow to fast throughout a set.
Listen for the Drum, Metal rattle.
The music is characterized by the steady, rhythmic pulse of a drum and the metallic shaking of rattles, punctuated by traditional singing and a distinct wolf-like howl.

Waveform or rhythm-pattern graphic: Alternating hard and soft drumbeats.

scenes.title: The costume and the setting
narration: Regalia includes a red and blue blanket, a skunk berry bandolier, and a metal rattle.
Dancers wear buckskin leggings and a long red breechcloth.
Head attire includes otter wraps or a roach.

scenes.title: The people
narration: Fred Tsoodle, Bill Koomsa, William Tanedooah, Clyde Ahtape, Harry Hall Zotigh, Fred Botone, Oliver Tanedooah, and Abel Big Bow.
Three main branches exist: the Kiowa Gourd Clan, the Tiah-Piah Society of Oklahoma, and the Kiowa TiaPiah Society of Carnegie.
The Gourd Dance is linked to the Kiowa warrior society Jài:fè:gàu (Tdeinpei-gah).

scenes.title: A respectful note
narration: The Gourd Dance is a sacred Kiowa tradition; outsiders should respect protocol, such as avoiding casual headwear like baseball caps or cowboy hats during the ceremony.
